gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-cambo: Commanding and wide, Amadeus stretches each word across the line without any tilt in its round letters. Cambo is the classic serif here, doing its work with a mellow swing from thick to thin that the heading never attempts.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-fanwood-text: Fanwood Text brings a literary, large-eyed lowercase, with curves that swell gently and gaps tiny enough to vanish at a glance. Amadeus, by contrast, spreads out wide and bold above it, and Fanwood Text keeps the reading quiet and bookish underneath.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-judson: Amadeus runs wide and monoline, its curves matching its stems with nothing tapered anywhere. And Judson is the opposite, a dignified classic serif with bulky small letters and hairlines that swing sharply away from its heavy stems.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-manuale: Amadeus stretches wide and bold, every curve as heavy as its stems and no tilt to the rounds. Manuale then softens things, its large-eyed lowercase tapering like a sharpened carpenter's pencil line, which gives the classic serif an editorial ease.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-naskh-arabic: One unbroken line runs through every glyph of Amadeus, wide-set and bold with no modulation at all. And Noto Naskh Arabic, a classic serif with a very tall x-height, feels like lightly engraved brass lettering set beside it: refined, settled and a touch slower.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-nastaliq-urdu: Noto Nastaliq Urdu reads tight and dignified, with little ascender height and a barely tilted calligraphy nib shaping each stroke. But Amadeus is just as striking on its own side, wide and bold with joins as heavy as its strokes, and that gap is the pair's whole appeal.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-rashi-hebrew: Amadeus is wide and rounded, a bold display face whose stroke ends never swell, so nothing about it softens. Noto Rashi Hebrew, a classic serif, would carry a long text gently, its brass-engraved contrast easing slowly from thick to thin.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-ahom: Amadeus keeps every stroke one width. Noto Serif Ahom, a classic serif, does the opposite job, with lofty tall lowercase and brush-like joins that taper modestly, while the heading simply commands the line with wide, bold words.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-armenia: Noto Serif Armenian reads traditional and authoritative, with big open counters in every small letter and a mild stroke contrast like engraved brass. And Amadeus does what it does best, stretching bold words wide at one thickness throughout, while the serif handles the finer detail.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-balines: Plain unmodulated outlines, stretched wide and bold, make Amadeus instantly recognizable. Noto Serif Balinese sits next to it with tall, vertical lowercase and a middle-of-the-road contrast, so the pair feels editorial and traditional, one loud and one measured.
